# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH ENTEROCOCCI

Enterococcus faecalis is almost always susceptible to penicillins locally, ampicillin is more effective than vancomycin in susceptible isolates.

Enterococcus faecium is typically resistant to some beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, and vancomycin. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.
[Approach to Endocarditis](endocarditis-approach-to)

# Duration of treatment

For uncomplicated infections where blood cultures are sterile after 24 hours of treatment, treat for 7-14 days. A longer duration is needed if infection is complicated or repeat blood cultures are positive.

Therapy:
## Treatment of susceptible E. Faecalis (Van A/B negative)

Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R

## Treatment of susceptible E. Faecium (Van A/B negative)

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

## Treatment of resistant enterococcus (Van A/B positive)

Linezolid 600 mg IV q12h ($$$$) DI
